claim: Trypanosoma brucei undergoes a complex life cycle in the tsetse fly.
source: The highly motile and versatile protozoan pathogen Trypanosoma brucei undergoes a complex life cycle in the tsetse fly.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by the detailed descriptions and observations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Multicolour light sheet fluorescence microscopy provided information about tsetse tissue topology with unprecedented resolution.
source: Multicolour light sheet fluorescence microscopy provided information about tsetse tissue topology with unprecedented resolution and allowed the first 3D analysis of the infection process.
evidence: The manuscript describes the application of LSFM and presents 3D reconstructions and images demonstrating high-resolution tissue topology.

claim: This work allowed the first 3D analysis of the trypanosome infection process in tsetse flies.
source: Multicolour light sheet fluorescence microscopy provided information about tsetse tissue topology with unprecedented resolution and allowed the first 3D analysis of the infection process.
evidence: The manuscript presents novel 3D reconstructions of infected tsetse tissues using LSFM, which had not been done before.

claim: Trypanosomes exhibit versatile behaviour ranging from solitary motion and near-wall swimming to collective motility in synchronised swarms.
source: High-speed fluorescence microscopy illuminated the versatile behaviour of trypanosome developmental stages, ranging from solitary motion and near-wall swimming to collective motility in synchronised swarms and in confinement.
evidence: The manuscript provides high-speed microscopy data and videos showing different types of trypanosome motility behaviors.

claim: Leeuwenhoek observed animalcules more than 300 years ago.
source: More than 300 years ago, Leeuwenhoek not only observed free swimming organisms, but also studied ´animalcules´ from animal and human environments, especially the fate of spermatozoa in the female genital tract (Leeuwenhoek, 1685).
evidence: This is a historical fact cited from Leeuwenhoek's work in 1685.

claim: Model systems for the study of microswimmers in their natural habitats are few and far between.
source: Still, to the present day, model systems for the study of microswimmers in their natural habitats are few and far between.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field, supported by the context of the introduction.

claim: The physical properties of the female genital tract are significant for sperm motility and fertilisation success.
source: The significance of the physical properties of the female genital tract for sperm motility and internal fertilisation success has been recognised (Fauci and Dillon, 2006; Kirkman-Brown and Smith, 2011), but this system naturally remains challenging for in vivo analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The female genital tract system remains challenging for in vivo analysis.
source: The significance of the physical properties of the female genital tract for sperm motility and internal fertilisation success has been recognised (Fauci and Dillon, 2006; Kirkman-Brown and Smith, 2011), but this system naturally remains challenging for in vivo analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the sperm model system.

claim: E. coli is a major microswimmer model.
source: Another major microswimmer model is E. coli.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field of microswimmer research.

claim: The rotating prokaryotic flagellar apparatus has been intensively studied to unravel mechanisms of chemotaxis.
source: The rotating prokaryotic flagellar apparatus has been intensively studied, mainly in order to unravel the mechanisms of chemotaxis (Micali and Endres, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: There is great interest in the collective behaviour of prokaryotes and the implications of real life surroundings.
source: Recently, there is great interest in the collective behaviour of prokaryotes and the implications of real life surroundings, as cells seldom stay alone or move without encountering mechanical obstructions for long periods of time (Chaban et al., 2015; Persat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: Bacterial collectives constitute relevant ecosystems as biofilms or intestinal microbiomes.
source: In fact, bacterial collectives constitute relevant ecosystems themselves, that is as biofilms or intestinal microbiomes (Ben-Jacob et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Chlamydomonas has been used as a model organism for analysis of phototaxis, ultrastructural characterisation of the axonemal system and analysis of intraflagellar transport.
source: Several free swimming protists, pre-eminently the green alga Chlamydomonas, have been used as model organisms during the last century, for the analysis of phototaxis, ultrastructural characterisation of the axonemal system and analysis of intraflagellar transport, to name only a few important topics (Simon and Plattner, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The life cycles of important parasitic protists have been recognised since the late nineteenth century.
source: The life cycles of important parasitic protists, including the agents of malaria, Chaga´s disease and African sleeping sickness have been recognised since the late nineteenth century (Leadbeater and McCready, 2000).
evidence: This is a historical fact supported by a citation.

claim: African trypanosomes were amongst the first blood parasites to be observed.
source: African trypanosomes were amongst the first blood parasites to be observed '…, wriggling about like tiny eels and swimming from corpuscle to corpuscle, which they seem to seize upon and worry.' (Bruce et al., 1895).
evidence: This is a historical observation cited from Bruce et al., 1895.

claim: The full developmental cycle of trypanosomes, involving transmission by the tsetse fly vector, was described.
source: The flagellates were found in blood, tissues and cerebrospinal fluid of various animal species and humans, and their full developmental cycle, involving transmission by the tsetse fly vector, was subsequently described (summarised in [Steverding, 2008]).
evidence: This is a historical fact supported by a citation.

claim: Trypanosomes have become important model organisms due to their medical importance and fascinating cell biology.
source: Since then, trypanosomes have become important model organisms, due to their medical importance and fascinating cell biology, including distinctive genetic features and multifaceted developmental stages (Hoare, 1972; Matthews, 2015; Vickerman et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The exact swimming mechanism of Trypanosoma brucei has only recently been elucidated.
source: Although trypanosomes have always fascinated as microswimmers, the exact swimming mechanism of Trypanosoma brucei has only recently been elucidated (Heddergott et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent research.

claim: The greater part of the trypanosome flagellum is attached to the cell body, winding around it in a helical course.
source: The parasite is unusual among the flagellates, as the greater part of the flagellum is attached to the cell body, winding around it in a helical course.
evidence: This is a morphological description supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The flagellum produces waves from both ends of the elastic cell body, which let the cells tumble and twist, producing the wriggling or corkscrew-like trypanosome movement.
source: The flagellum produces waves from both ends of the elastic cell body, which let the cells tumble and twist, producing the wriggling or corkscrew-like trypanosome movement, typically observed in culture media or blood smears.
evidence: This is a description of trypanosome motility supported by previous research and observations.

claim: The mechanical parameters of the surroundings influence the parasite's motile behaviour.
source: Importantly, the mechanical parameters of the surroundings, that is fluid viscosity or presence of obstacles, influence the parasite's motile behaviour, affecting the frequency ratio of bidirectional flagellar beating and inducing persistent unidirectional movement (Heddergott et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Trypanosomes seem to have evolved to be highly versatile swimmers, adapted to react flexibly to different mechanical properties of various microenvironments.
source: Thus, trypanosomes seem to have evolved to be highly versatile swimmers, adapted to react flexibly to different mechanical properties of various microenvironments.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed motility behaviors and adaptations.

claim: Different trypanosome species exhibited a species-specific dynamic adjustment of motile behaviour to various physical surroundings.
source: The parasites exhibited a species-specific dynamic adjustment of motile behaviour to various physical surroundings, which could correlate with their preferred infection niches within their mammalian hosts (Bargul et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The importance of specific niches during infection has been recognised and is currently being scrutinised.
source: The importance of specific niches during infection has been recognised and is currently being scrutinised (Caljon et al., 2016; Capewell et al., 2016; Trindade et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: Accessible and controllable in vitro and in vivo systems are in demand for studying collective swimming behaviour and the influence of borders and confinement.
source: As the interest of biological and especially physical research is focusing on collective swimming behaviour and the influence of borders and confinement, accessible and controllable in vitro and in vivo systems are in demand (Elgeti and Gompper, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: This work describes the first enclosed host-parasite system that is amenable to highly detailed analysis of diverse microswimmers in defined microenvironments.
source: To this effect we describe here the first enclosed host-parasite system that is amenable to highly detailed analysis of diverse microswimmers in defined microenvironments.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the system presented in the manuscript.

claim: T. brucei is taken up by the tsetse fly during a blood meal.
source: T. brucei is taken up by the tsetse fly during a blood meal, whereupon the parasites undergo a complex developmental cycle, while traversing various organs of the tsetse´s alimentary tract (Ooi and Bastin, 2013; Rotureau and Van Den Abbeele, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The development of trypanosomes in the tsetse fly involves several genetically fixed physiological changes.
source: The development involves several genetically fixed physiological changes, allowing the adaptation to significantly different host compartments and striking morphological changes, which greatly influence motile behaviour.
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in the manuscript and previous research.

claim: Motility is necessary for successful infection and transmission back to the mammalian host.
source: Motility is necessary for successful infection and transmission back to the mammalian host (Rotureau et al., 2014) and might be of paramount importance for passing several 'bottlenecks' in trypanosome development (Dyer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The trypanosome-tsetse system is particularly attractive for studying flagellate microswimmers in their natural habitats.
source: We consider the trypanosome-tsetse system as particularly attractive for studying flagellate microswimmers in their natural habitats.
evidence: This is an assertion made by the authors based on the characteristics of the system.

claim: The small size of the insect allows measurements of trypanosome swimming behaviour at very different scales.
source: The small size of the insect allows measurements of trypanosome swimming behaviour at very different scales, ranging from the observation of all parasites in whole flies to single cell analyses with high spatiotemporal resolution.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Light sheet fluorescence microscopy was adapted to map the tsetse fly's internal topology.
source: For this purpose, we adapted light sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) to map the tsetse fly´s internal topology.
evidence: This is described in the methods and results sections.

claim: LSFM technology allowed recording of high resolution optical sections of complete fly body parts and generation of three-dimensional reconstructions of intact tissues.
source: This technology allowed us to record high resolution optical sections of complete fly body parts and generate three-dimensional reconstructions of intact tissues.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the images and 3D models presented in the manuscript.

claim: Multicolour LSFM simultaneously localised epithelial tissues via autofluorescence, the peritrophic matrix through rhodamine-labelled wheat germ agglutinin, and the infecting trypanosomes by GFP-expression in the nucleus.
source: Multicolour LSFM simultaneously localised epithelial tissues via autofluorescence, the peritrophic matrix (PM) through rhodamine-labelled wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) and the infecting trypanosomes by GFP-expression in the nucleus.
evidence: This is described in the methods and demonstrated in the figures.

claim: The peritrophic matrix is a non-cellular, glycosaminoglycan, glycoprotein and chitin containing, cylindrical sleeve that continuously lines the gut epithelium.
source: The PM is a non-cellular, glycosaminoglycan, glycoprotein and chitin containing, cylindrical sleeve, that continuously lines the gut epithelium and acts as a physical barrier for pathogens ingested within the blood meal (Lehane et al., 1996; Lehane, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The peritrophic matrix acts as a physical barrier for pathogens ingested within the blood meal.
source: The PM is a non-cellular, glycosaminoglycan, glycoprotein and chitin containing, cylindrical sleeve, that continuously lines the gut epithelium and acts as a physical barrier for pathogens ingested within the blood meal (Lehane et al., 1996; Lehane, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The peritrophic matrix showed an astonishing degree of convolution in both gut regions after the fly had completed digestion.
source: After the fly had completed digestion, the PM showed an astonishing degree of convolution in both gut regions, the full extent of which can be appreciated in single slices (Figure 2, bottom panel, Video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM images and 3D reconstructions in Figure 2 and Video 2.

claim: The peritrophic matrix was folded extensively, producing a multitude of channels, folds and crevices, thereby increasing the absolute surface area.
source: The PM was folded extensively, producing a multitude of channels, folds and crevices, thereby increasing the absolute surface area.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM images and 3D reconstructions.

claim: The diameter and surface area of the peritrophic matrix significantly increased towards the posterior part of the midgut.
source: The diameter and thus the surface area of the sleeve significantly increased towards the posterior part of the midgut (Figure 2B), allowing the PM to adapt to the extreme swelling of the gut during a blood meal.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM images in Figure 2B.

claim: The developmental progress of the fluorescent protein-expressing pleomorphic AnTat1.1 cell lines through all morphological stages was confirmed, including the final production of mammalian-infective stages.
source: We confirmed the developmental progress of the fluorescent protein-expressing pleomorphic AnTat1.1 cell lines through all morphological stages, including the final production of mammalian-infective stages (metacyclic form, Figure 3 - Video 1 and Figure 3 - Video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the videos showing metacyclic cells.

claim: A spatiotemporal map of the mean abundance of parasites shows the characteristic establishment of an early posterior midgut infection, the diminishing of populations between days four and six, and the invasion of the anterior midgut and the proventriculus from day seven on.
source: A spatiotemporal map of the mean abundance of parasites shows the characteristic establishment of an early posterior midgut infection, the diminishing of populations between days four and six and the invasion of the anterior midgut and the proventriculus from day seven on (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the heat map in Figure 3A.

claim: After days six to seven, the transmission of the parasites depends on developmental stages that cross the peritrophic matrix and colonise the ectoperitrophic space to migrate to the foregut.
source: After days six to seven, the transmission of the parasites depends on developmental stages that cross the PM and colonise the ectoperitrophic space to migrate to the foregut (Gibson and Bailey, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: LSFM is well suited to determine the in situ parasite population status in body tissues of arbitrarily complex geometries, with single cell resolution.
source: Our results show that LSFM is well suited to determine the in situ parasite population status in body tissues of arbitrarily complex geometries, with single cell resolution (Figure 3—Video 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The bacteriome is a conspicuous region adjacent to the anterior midgut of the fly, containing essential endosymbiotic bacteria, particularly the obligate mutualist Wigglesworthia.
source: The bacteriome is a conspicuous region adjacent to the anterior midgut of the fly, containing essential endosymbiotic bacteria, particularly the obligate mutualist Wigglesworthia, which resides intracellularly in bacteriocytes (Aksoy, 1995; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The proventriculus is an intricately shaped organ connecting the anterior midgut, the crop and the salivary duct.
source: The proventriculus is an intricately shaped organ connecting the anterior midgut, the crop and the salivary duct (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM images in Figure 4B.

claim: The peritrophic matrix is synthesised within specialised cells of the proventriculus and pushed rapidly into the anterior midgut region.
source: The PM is synthesised within these specialised cells and pushed rapidly into the anterior midgut region.
evidence: This is a known fact about the peritrophic matrix.

claim: It is unknown if trypanosomes are able to cross the peritrophic matrix at the proventriculus, or how they traverse the proventriculus and continue on their journey to the salivary glands.
source: As it is unknown if trypanosomes are able to cross the PM here, or how they traverse the proventriculus and continue on their journey to the salivary glands, this region is currently being intensely studied (Rose et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as an open question in the field, supported by a citation.

claim: The characterisation of trypanosomes three dimensional cell body shape and the attachment conformation of their force-producing flagella has been important in elucidating the parasites precise swimming mechanism.
source: The characterisation of trypanosomes three dimensional cell body shape and the attachment conformation of their force-producing flagella, has been important in elucidating the parasites precise swimming mechanism (Heddergott et al., 2012), the characterisation of species-specific differences in motile behaviour (Bargul et al., 2016), as well as the numeric simulation of the microswimmers motility in a hydrodynamic surrounding (Alizadehrad et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Eight different developmental (transition) stages were analysed, excluding only epimastigote trypanosomes attached to the epithelium of the salivary glands and the long epimastigote stage that presumably degenerates after asymmetric division.
source: Eight different developmental (transition) stages were analysed, excluding only epimastigote trypanosomes attached to the epithelium of the salivary glands and the long epimastigote stage that presumably degenerates after asymmetric division.
evidence: This is stated in the description of the morphometric analysis.

claim: None of the life cycle stages revealed an undulating membrane.
source: None of the life cycle stages revealed an undulating membrane, which corroborates the finding that propulsion of bloodstream form trypanosomes is solely accomplished by flagellar beating according to resistive force theory, because the membranes of flagellum and cell body are directly adjacent and do not form an extended, fin-like appendage (Heddergott et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on the morphometric analysis and supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Propulsion of bloodstream form trypanosomes is solely accomplished by flagellar beating according to resistive force theory.
source: None of the life cycle stages revealed an undulating membrane, which corroborates the finding that propulsion of bloodstream form trypanosomes is solely accomplished by flagellar beating according to resistive force theory, because the membranes of flagellum and cell body are directly adjacent and do not form an extended, fin-like appendage (Heddergott et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The procyclic trypanosomes develop in the gut lumen from the cell cycle arrested stumpy bloodstream form.
source: The procyclic trypanosomes (PCF) (Figure 5A) develop in the gut lumen from the cell cycle arrested stumpy BSF (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is a known fact about trypanosome development.

claim: Compared to the bloodstream forms, the procyclic cells have elongated and thinned considerably.
source: Compared to the bloodstream forms, the procyclic cells have elongated and thinned considerably.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figure 5.

claim: The flagellum of procyclic cells describes a 180° right hand turn around the cell body progressing towards the anterior end.
source: The flagellum describes a 180° right hand turn around the cell body progressing towards the anterior end.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the 3D morphometric analysis in Figure 5A.

claim: The rotation frequency of procyclic parasites is similar to that of bloodstream form cells.
source: The rotation frequency of procyclic parasites is similar to that of BSF cells, albeit the rotation is easier to observe in the latter as the flagellar wave travels to the posterior end and deforms the whole length of the elastic cell body, giving BSF swimmers a smoother appearing auger-like trajectory, which was eponymous for the parasite.
evidence: This is based on the waveform analysis presented in Figure 6.

claim: The long procyclic cells had elongated and thinned further, without changing the attachment conformation of the flagellum.
source: The long procyclic trypanosomes isolated from the flies had elongated and thinned further, without changing the attachment conformation of the flagellum.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Long procyclic trypanosomes maintain a slightly higher frequency and amplitude of flagellar oscillation compared to procyclic cells.
source: The long procyclic trypanosomes maintain a slightly higher frequency and amplitude of flagellar oscillation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6B.

claim: Long procyclic cells reach more than double the speed of the shorter procyclic form.
source: Together with the increased absolute length of the flagellum, these parameters allow the long procyclic to reach more than double the speed of the shorter form.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the speed measurements in Figure 6.

claim: The development of cell cycle-arrested mesocyclic cells is characterised by the disappearance of the free flagellar part at the anterior end, due to further elongation of the cell body.
source: The development of cell cycle-arrested mesocyclic cells is characterised by the disappearance of the free flagellar part at the anterior end, due to further elongation of the cell body (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figure 5C.

claim: The transition to the cellular waveform of mesocyclic cells is characterised by a switch to traveling waves of smaller amplitude and wavelength.
source: The transition to the cellular waveform of mesocyclic cells is characterised by a switch to traveling waves of smaller amplitude and wavelength (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6C.

claim: Despite constant beat frequency and further increased flagellar length, swimming speed of mesocyclic cells is slightly reduced compared to long procyclic cells.
source: Despite constant beat frequency and further increased flagellar length, swimming speed is slightly reduced.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6C.

claim: The lack of a free anterior part of the flagellum is most likely responsible for the characteristic change of waveform in mesocyclic cells and results in very straight swimming trajectories.
source: The lack of a free anterior part of the flagellum is most likely responsible for the characteristic change of waveform and results in very straight swimming trajectories.
evidence: This is an inference based on the morphometric and waveform analyses.

claim: The transformation of mesocyclic cells into epimastigote forms occurs by a continuous repositioning of the cell nucleus from the anterior to the posterior side of the kinetoplast, followed by re-entry into the cell cycle.
source: The transformation of mesocyclic cells into epimastigote forms occurs by a continuous repositioning of the cell nucleus from the anterior to the posterior side of the kinetoplast, followed by re-entry into the cell cycle (Hoare and Wallace, 1966; Sharma et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: During the transition from mesocyclic to epimastigote parasites, a continuously larger part of the anterior flagellum protrudes, which results in higher amplitude waves being initiated by the free flagellar tip.
source: During the transition from mesocyclic to epimastigote parasites, a continuously larger part of the anterior flagellum protrudes, which results in higher amplitude waves being initiated by the free flagellar tip (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6D.

claim: While the flagellar length only increases slightly during the mesocyclic to epimastigote transition, the beat frequency doubles, allowing the transition stages to reach speeds above 100 µm/s.
source: While the flagellar length only increases slightly, the beat frequency doubles, allowing the transition stages to reach speeds above 100 µm/s.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6D.

claim: The epimastigotes possess a virtually completely free flagellum, producing large amplitude waves that travel unhindered to the posterior cell body, enabling them to be pulled at speeds well above 100 µm/s.
source: The epimastigotes possess a virtually completely free flagellum (Figure 5E), producing large amplitude waves that travel unhindered to the posterior cell body, enabling to be pulled at speeds well above 100 µm/s (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric and waveform analyses in Figures 5E and 6E.

claim: The epimastigote cell divides asymmetrically to produce a long and a short epimastigote.
source: The epimastigote cell divides asymmetrically to produce a long and a short epimastigote (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figure 5F.

claim: The short epimastigote cells are characterised by a rudimentary flagellum attached anteriorly to a thin and stiff cell body.
source: The short epimastigote cells are characterised by a rudimentary flagellum attached anteriorly to a thin and stiff cell body (Figures 5F and 6F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figures 5F and 6F.

claim: The short epimastigote cell does not reach speeds above 10 µm/s, as there is no appreciable travelling wave propagated.
source: The flagellum is capable of regular oscillation and persistent movement, but the cell does not reach speeds above 10 µm/s, as there is no appreciable travelling wave propagated.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6F.

claim: Within one cell cycle, a very capable microswimmer produces an almost immotile parasite.
source: Thus, within one cell cycle, a very capable microswimmer produces an almost immotile parasite.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of epimastigote and short epimastigote motility.

claim: Metacyclic parasites reveal trypomastigote morphology, as the nucleus has repositioned to the anterior side of the kinetoplast.
source: Metacyclic parasites reveal trypomastigote morphology, as the nucleus has repositioned to the anterior side of the kinetoplast (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figure 5G.

claim: Metacyclic parasites swim freely in the saliva and represent the infective form that is pre-adapted to survive in the mammalian host.
source: They swim freely in the saliva and represent the infective form that is pre-adapted to survive in the mammalian host (Otieno and Darji, 1979) (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The elastic cell body of metacyclic cells deforms in the shape of the flagellar waveform.
source: The cell body appears elastic and is deformed in the shape of the flagellar waveform.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6G.

claim: The flagellum of metacyclic cells emerges at the very posterior end and has once more adopted the right hand 180° turn around the cell body.
source: The flagellum emerges at the very posterior end and has once more adopted the right hand 180° turn around the cell body.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morphometric analysis in Figure 5G.

claim: The flagellar tip of metacyclic cells produces waves of high amplitude with frequencies similar to procyclic parasites.
source: The flagellar tip produces waves of high amplitude with frequencies similar to procyclic parasites.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the waveform analysis in Figure 6G.

claim: The steep chiral course of the attached flagellum in metacyclic cells produces relatively high rotational forces, which result in a contracted cellular waveform, reducing forward swimming speed.
source: A travelling wave propagates along the cell body, but the steep chiral course of the attached flagellum produces relatively high rotational forces, which result in a contracted cellular waveform, reducing forward swimming speed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the waveform analysis in Figure 6G.

claim: Following transmission to the mammalian host, the metacylic stage differentiates to the slender bloodstream stage.
source: Following transmission to the mammalian host, the metacylic stage differentiates to the slender bloodstream stage.
evidence: This is a known fact about trypanosome development.

claim: The slender bloodstream population produces the fly infective stumpy bloodstream form.
source: The cycle begins anew when the slender population produces the fly infective stumpy bloodstream form (Figure 5I) (Vickerman, 1985).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: During their journey through the various organs and tissues of the tsetse fly trypanosomes pass developmental 'bottlenecks'.
source: During their journey through the various organs and tissues of the tsetse fly trypanosomes pass developmental 'bottlenecks' (Dyer et al., 2013; Oberle et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: After their uptake by the tsetse fly, the trypanosomes swim freely between blood cells in the gut lumen.
source: After their uptake by the tsetse fly, the trypanosomes swim freely between blood cells in the gut lumen (Figure 7A, Video 7).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 7A and Video 7.

claim: The bloodstream form ingested with the mammalian host blood transform into procyclic form in the tsetse gut lumen.
source: Here, the BSF, ingested with the mammalian host blood, transform into PCF.
evidence: This is a known fact about trypanosome development.

claim: A typical procyclic trypanosome swam persistently with an average speed of 69 µm/s and a flagellar beat frequency of 25 Hz.
source: The cell marked in Figure 7A, for example, represents a typical procyclic trypanosome, which swam persistently with an average speed of 69 µm/s and a flagellar beat frequency of 25 Hz (Video 7).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy analysis in Figure 7A and Video 7.

claim: Trypanosomes can reverse the flagellar beat in order to change direction and move forward along a new path when experiencing mechanical hindrance.
source: It swam slowly with reduced amplitude, was repeatedly halted, and reversed the flagellar beat in order to change direction and move forward along a new path (Video 7). This behaviour is characteristic also for BSF trypanosomes that experience mechanical hindrance, and is postulated to allow the parasites to escape from dead ends, for example in confined tissue spaces (Heddergott et al., 2012).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy and supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: After reaching the ectoperitrophic space, the procyclic cells continue development by transforming into the cell cycle arrested mesocyclic stage.
source: After reaching the ectoperitrophic space, the procyclic cells continue development by transforming into the cell cycle arrested mesocyclic stage.
evidence: This is a known fact about trypanosome development.

claim: Mesocyclic parasites are capable of sharp U-turns, due to their highly flexible cell body.
source: Mesocyclic parasites are also capable of sharp U-turns, due to their highly flexible cell body (Figure 8C, Video 8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 8C and Video 8.

claim: Some mesocyclic cells eventually navigate through the ectoperitrophic space to the proventriculus, where they undergo a continuous transition to the thin epimastigote cells.
source: Some mesocyclic cells eventually navigate through the ectoperitrophic space to the proventriculus, where they undergo a continuous transition to the thin epimastigote cells, which are propelled by a sperm-like, long free flagellum.
evidence: This is a known fact about trypanosome development.

claim: The dividing epimastigote stage is believed to be a piggyback transporter for the developmentally relevant short epimastigote cells.
source: For this reason, the dividing epimastigote stage is believed to be a piggyback transporter for the developmentally relevant short epimastigote cells, although this route to the salivary glands has not been demonstrated so far (Sharma et al., 2008; Van Den Abbeele et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Metacyclic cells tumbled, meaning they frequently reversed flagellar beats and effectively stayed in one place in the salivary duct.
source: The cells tumbled, meaning they frequently reversed flagellar beats and effectively stayed in one place.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 7E and Video 7E.

claim: The tumbling behavior of metacyclic cells in the salivary duct could be expected to be normal in vivo behaviour, as the infective form lingers in the salivary glands for the next blood meal of the tsetse fly.
source: This could be expected to be normal in vivo behaviour for the infective metacyclic form, as it lingers in the salivary glands for the next blood meal of the tsetse fly, which will inject the parasite into a vertebrate host.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed behavior and the biology of the parasite.

claim: The solitary swimming behaviour of all trypanosome development stages is massively influenced by the microenvironment, especially by way of confinement and presence of boundary layers.
source: The above data illustrate that the solitary swimming behaviour of all trypanosome development stages is massively influenced by the microenvironment, especially by way of confinement and presence of boundary layers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the high-speed microscopy observations.

claim: Near-wall motion is a prominent feature of mesocyclic microswimmers.
source: Near-wall motion is a prominent feature of mesocyclic microswimmers, which not only is biologically relevant, but also provides theoretical physics with an example of a natural near-wall swimmer.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy observations.

claim: Tsetse trypanosomes show highly coordinated collective motion behaviours, over a large range of cell concentrations and in a multitude of variably confining microenvironments.
source: While tsetse trypanosomes can be observed as solitary swimmers, they also show highly coordinated collective motion behaviours, over a large range of cell concentrations and in a multitude of variably confining microenvironments (Figure 8, Video 8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 8 and Video 8.

claim: Groups of trypanosomes frequently synchronised their flagellar beats.
source: Interestingly, those groups of cells frequently synchronised their flagellar beats.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy observations.

claim: Procyclic parasites can synchronise their oscillations and also reverse their flagellar beat to leave the cluster.
source: Cells swam forward to join the group and synchronised, but also reversed their flagellar beat, which resulted in backward motion to leave the cluster (Video 8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Video 8.

claim: At very high densities, mesocyclic cells were seen to fill large interstitial spaces and produce superordinate wave patterns.
source: At very high densities, especially mesocyclic cells were seen to fill large interstitial spaces. The cells were packed closely, continuously oscillating and obscuring most details of the surrounding tissue (Figure 8D, Video 8). Several regions were visible where the tips of trypanosomes seemed to converge and began to synchronise their flagellar waves. Large numbers of trypanosomes gathered around these centres and produced superordinate wave patterns.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 8D and Video 8.

claim: Collective motion of mesocyclic cells was seen to move a part of the tissue, thus apparently producing significant directional force.
source: This collective motion was even seen to move a part of the tissue, thus apparently producing significant directional force.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy observations.

claim: High-speed microscopy of fluorescent reporter trypanosomes allowed the quantitative analysis of single cell motion within swarms and the identification of the life cycle stage of the individual parasites.
source: High-speed microscopy of fluorescent reporter trypanosomes thus not only allowed the quantitative analysis of single cell motion within swarms, but also the identification of the life cycle stage of the individual parasites (Figure 9, Video 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed fluorescence microscopy in Figure 9 and Video 9.

claim: Procyclic parasites have a round nucleus, whereas mesocyclic trypanosomes feature an elongated nucleus.
source: Procyclic parasites have a round nucleus, whereas mesocyclic trypanosomes feature an elongated nucleus.
evidence: This is a known morphological characteristic used for identification.

claim: During the mesocyclic to epimastigote transition, the nucleus elongates further to assume a more rod-shaped appearance.
source: During the mesocyclic to epimastigote transition, the nucleus elongates further to assume a more rod-shaped appearance (Sharma et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The average speeds of persistently swimming cells in tsetse tissues were measured to be around 15–25 µm/s, with the highest speeds of around 40 µm/s measured in fluid filled spaces.
source: The average speeds of persistently swimming cells in these tissues were measured to be around 15–25 µm/s (colour coded in Figure 9A3–C3), with the highest speeds of around 40 µm/s measured in fluid filled spaces (red tracks in Figure 9C3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the tracking analysis in Figure 9.

claim: Single cells could be traced swimming into the flock, where they synchronise with the stationary oscillatory movements of the surrounding trypanosomes, eventually reverse the flagellar beat and leave again.
source: Notably, single cells could be traced swimming into the flock, where they synchronise with the stationary oscillatory movements of the surrounding trypanosomes, eventually reverse the flagellar beat and leave again (Video 9C2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the tracking analysis in Video 9C2.

claim: The synchronisation of trypanosome groups indicates the self-organisation of the assemblies by hydrodynamic forces.
source: This indicates the self-organisation of the assemblies by hydrodynamic forces.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed behavior.

claim: The journey of trypanosomes through the tsetse fly is marked by successions of solitary and collective motion patterns.
source: The experiments so far demonstrated that the journey of trypanosomes through the tsetse fly is marked by successions of solitary and collective motion patterns.
evidence: This is a summary of the observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The distinct life cycle stages are differentially equipped for their journey through the tsetse fly, which is reflected in their cellular waveforms.
source: The distinct life cycle stages are differentially equipped for this endeavour, which is reflected in their cellular waveforms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the morphometric and waveform analyses.

claim: Procyclic trypanosomes have been shown to perform social motility in vitro, albeit in a manner probably controlled by chemosensing and over long time scales.
source: Procyclic trypanosomes have been shown to perform social motility in vitro, albeit in a manner probably controlled by chemosensing and over long time scales (Imhof et al., 2014; Oberholzer et al., 2010, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A chemical process for synchronisation would be reaction-diffusion driven, and hence, should generally be slower than sensing by hydrodynamic interactions.
source: A chemical process would be reaction-diffusion driven, and hence, should generally be slower than sensing by hydrodynamic interactions.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration based on physical principles.

claim: Synchronised motion patterns were observed to form and disperse spontaneously.
source: In fact, we observed synchronised motion patterns to form and disperse spontaneously (Figure 10, Video 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 10 and Video 10.

claim: A spontaneous synchronisation event was observed where all cells in a region were seen beating in one direction, apparently constricted at the narrow corner of the epithelial border.
source: In one of these regions we recorded an alignment of cells several seconds later, where all cells in the region were seen beating in one direction, apparently constricted at the narrow corner of the epithelial border. The cells had arranged in a swarm conformation that was stable for at least several minutes (Figure 10A right, Video 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 10A and Video 10.

claim: The trigger for the spontaneous synchronisation event was unlikely of chemical nature, but rather a shift in the surroundings of the dissected specimen.
source: The trigger for this spontaneous synchronisation event was unlikely of chemical nature, but rather a shift in the surroundings of the dissected specimen, which could have changed the volume of, or the pressure on the parasite-harbouring space.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timescale of the observed event.

claim: The reversal of a synchronised swarm into an isotropic distribution of swimming cells was observed on a timescale of seconds.
source: In another recording of synchronised cells with fluorescent flagellar markers (Figure 10B left, Video 10), the reversal of such a swarm into an isotropic distribution of swimming cells was observed, also on a timescale of seconds (Figure 10B right, Video 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy in Figure 10B and Video 10.

claim: The collective behaviour of large trypanosome populations can be self-organised by hydrodynamic interactions without the need for any physical attachment to tissues.
source: These results showed unambiguously that the collective behaviour of large trypanosome populations can be self-organised by hydrodynamic interactions without the need for any physical attachment to tissues, as had been shown for small groups of cells (e.g. Figure 8A–B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observations of spontaneous synchronisation and desynchronisation.

claim: The timescale of a few seconds observed for collective organisational status change is significantly smaller than the shortest known timescale of potential chemotactic behaviour in trypanosomes.
source: It should be noted, that the timescale of a few seconds observed here for collective organisational status change is significantly smaller than the shortest known timescale of potential chemotactic behaviour in trypanosomes (Oberholzer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: An adaptive reaction system required for directed behaviour of parasite swarms is unlikely to be responsible for establishing the switching behaviour observed in the experiments.
source: Although chemical signals will undoubtedly be relevant for rapid fluctuations of flagellar beating, an adaptive reaction system required for directed behaviour of parasite swarms is unlikely to be responsible for establishing the switching behaviour observed in our experiments.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timescale of the observed events.

claim: The ability of mesocyclic forms for near-wall swimming and to form huge and dense clusters or swarms, without apparent attachments, is a distinctive feature, indicating the capacity for hydrodynamic self-organisation.
source: The ability of mesocyclic forms for near-wall swimming and to form huge and dense clusters or swarms, without apparent attachments, is a distinctive feature, indicating the capacity for hydrodynamic self-organisation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The performance of microbial swimmers could be shaped by their microenvironment, very much in the same way as is the natural swimming behaviour of large animals.
source: It is a still comparatively neglected possibility that the performance of microbial swimmers could be shaped by their microenvironment, very much in the same way as is the natural swimming behaviour of large animals.
evidence: This is a general statement about the potential influence of the environment on microswimmer behavior.

claim: We lack defined natural model environments for motion at low Reynolds numbers.
source: Understanding microswimmer behaviour is less straightforward, mainly because we lack defined natural model environments for motion at low Reynolds numbers.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field.

claim: The extended and developmentally programmed succession of microswimmers in different body parts of a small-sized insect like the tsetse fly provides a tractable model for studying microswimmers in natural environments.
source: The extended and developmentally programmed succession of microswimmers in different body parts of a small-sized insect like the tsetse fly provides such a tractable model.
evidence: This is a claim about the utility of the tsetse-trypanosome system.

claim: Multicolour LSFM allowed three-dimensional reconstruction of basically any region of the fly habitat with a resolution sufficient to visualise individual fluorescent trypanosomes, concomitant with the mapping of tissue structures in intact organs.
source: Multicolour LSFM allowed us to three-dimensionally reconstruct basically any region of the fly habitat with a resolution sufficient to visualise individual fluorescent trypanosomes, concomitant with the mapping of tissue structures in intact organs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM data presented in the manuscript.

claim: LSFM produced astonishing views of the interior organisation of the fly gut, revealing the true topology of the peritrophic matrix to be extremely convoluted.
source: LSFM produced astonishing views of the interior organisation of the fly gut, revealing the true topology of the PM to be extremely convoluted.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM images and 3D reconstructions.

claim: The distension of the peritrophic matrix upon feeding and the extensive folding after excretion of liquid has been described elegantly in early work on Glossina.
source: This distension of the PM upon feeding and the extensive folding after excretion of liquid has been described elegantly in early work on Glossina (Wigglesworth, 1929).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Following publications on the peritrophic matrix did not appreciate the complexity of this environment.
source: Incomprehensibly, the following publications on the PM did not appreciate the complexity of this environment.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of previous research.

claim: A high-resolution, multi-colour, three-dimensional map of the complete peritrophic matrix and the trypanosomes therein was generated.
source: We generated a high-resolution, multi-colour, three-dimensional map of the complete PM and the trypanosomes therein.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The LSFM reconstructions enabled the assignment of the two-dimensional structures observed by live microscopy of the dissected organs.
source: The LSFM reconstructions also enabled the assignment of the two-dimensional structures observed by live microscopy of the dissected organs.
evidence: This is a methodological advantage of using LSFM.

claim: The spatial information gathered by LSFM yielded a quantitative assessment of the confinement states the parasites experience.
source: Importantly, the spatial information gathered by LSFM yielded a quantitative assessment of the confinement states the parasites experience.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LSFM data.

claim: The precise three-dimensional maps allow mathematic analyses of the degrees of confinement and connectivity within the peritrophic matrix maze.
source: The precise three-dimensional maps allow mathematic analyses of the degrees of confinement and connectivity within the PM maze.
evidence: This is a potential application of the LSFM data.

claim: The resultant data forms the basis for numerical simulations of single and collective swimming in this natural system of microchannels and crevices.
source: The resultant data forms the basis for numerical simulations of single and collective swimming in this natural system of microchannels and crevices.
evidence: This is a potential application of the data.

claim: In the living tsetse fly, the peritrophic matrix is not static but is dynamically folded and expanded during the digestion process.
source: In the living tsetse fly, the PM is not static but is dynamically folded and expanded during the digestion process.
evidence: This is a known fact about the peritrophic matrix.

claim: LSFM approaches for rapid live microscopy will be available.
source: Although this initially means an impediment to microscopic analysis, LSFM approaches for rapid live microscopy will be available (Heddleston and Chew, 2016) and the ability to record living microswimmers in such a complex, dynamic system will be an asset.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The LSFM measurements allowed instructive visualisations of the intact, parasite-infested proventriculus.
source: The LSFM measurements also allowed instructive visualisations of the intact, parasite-infested proventriculus (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM images in Figure 4B.

claim: The localisation of the proventricular trypanosome population revealed marked parasite concentration gradients along intact internal regions of the proventriculus.
source: The localisation of the proventricular trypanosome population revealed marked parasite concentration gradients along intact internal regions of the proventriculus.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the LSFM data.

claim: Microbe-surface interactions attract considerable attention because of their importance for sperm cells and bacteria.
source: Microbe-surface interactions attract considerable attention because of their importance for sperm cells and bacteria (Berke et al., 2008; Elgeti and Gompper, 2016; et al., 1963).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Sperm demonstrate a spiralling swimming trajectory that is modified by hydrodynamic and steric interactions at boundaries, resulting in rheotactic movement or surface slithering.
source: Sperm demonstrate a spiralling swimming trajectory that is modified by hydrodynamic and steric interactions at boundaries, resulting in rheotactic movement (Kantsler et al., 2014) or surface slithering, which might be beneficial under certain microenvironmental conditions (Nosrati et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The procyclic to mesocyclic trypanosome morphotypes appear to be adapted to swimming forwards in straight trajectories, which hardly change through contact with the peritrophic matrix.
source: In contrast, the procyclic to mesocyclic trypanosome morphotypes appear to be adapted to swimming forwards in straight trajectories, which hardly change through contact with the PM.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed behavior.

claim: Near-wall motion could be guiding the cells by influencing the persistence of forward movement.
source: Near-wall motion could rather be guiding the cells by influencing the persistence of forward movement, as the trypanosomes can readily reverse the direction of flagellar waves and perform turning manoeuvres (e.g. Video 7C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed behavior.

claim: Trypanosomes arguably have a higher degree of control in navigating along walls and through confined spaces than sperm or bacteria.
source: All in all, trypanosomes arguably have a higher degree of control in navigating along walls and through confined spaces than sperm or bacteria.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed capabilities of trypanosomes.

claim: Hydrodynamic synchronisation is a well-known phenomenon between sperm flagella and leads to higher order swarm behaviours.
source: Hydrodynamic synchronisation is a well-known phenomenon between sperm flagella ( et al., 1963; Yang et al., 2008) and leads to higher order swarm behaviours (Elgeti and Gompper, 2016; Immler et al., 2007; Riedel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The tsetse system allows the observation of all grades of collective accumulation, as distinct regions of the fly gut harbour different parasite concentrations.
source: The tsetse system allows the observation of all grades of collective accumulation, as distinct regions of the fly gut harbour different parasite concentrations.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The propensity to synchronise is dependent on specific developmental forms, allowing the study of variations on swarming behaviour with changing morphologies.
source: The propensity to synchronise is dependent on specific developmental forms, allowing the study of variations on swarming behaviour with changing morphologies.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the observations of different developmental stages.

claim: The trypanosomes' reverse swimming ability allows single swimmers to leave the collectives.
source: The trypanosomes add a further feature, as their reverse swimming ability allows single swimmers to leave the collectives.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the high-speed microscopy observations.

claim: Fluorescent parasites were generated in order to identify single trypanosomes in densely populated organs and tissues of the fly.
source: We have generated fluorescent parasites, in order to identify single trypanosomes in densely populated organs and tissues of the fly and demonstrate possibilities for quantitative tracking of cell nuclei and individual flagella, resolving cell motility to single flagellar beats.
evidence: This is described in the methods and demonstrated in the results.

claim: Using the tsetse-trypanosome system, we now have the so far unique ability to track single microswimmers of distinct developmentally regulated morphotypes within their natural microenvironments.
source: Thus, using the tsetse-trypanosome system, we now have the so far unique ability to track single microswimmers of distinct developmentally regulated morphotypes within their natural microenvironments.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty and utility of the system.

claim: The natural habitat poses an important challenge, as it will be necessary to elucidate the relevant physiochemical states prevailing for the parasite's developmental progression, in order to eventually establish complementary in vitro studies.
source: The natural habitat poses an important challenge though, as it will be necessary to elucidate the relevant physiochemical states prevailing for the parasite's developmental progression, in order to eventually establish complementary in vitro studies.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Microfluidic systems have been established for the analysis of bacteria and sperm research.
source: For this purpose microfluidic systems have been established, especially for the analysis of bacteria (Wu and Dekker, 2016) and sperm research (Knowlton et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Few microfluidic studies have focussed on microswimming and the elucidation of natural environmental factors.
source: Used mainly for biotechnological applications, few studies have focussed on microswimming and the elucidation of natural environmental factors (Hochstetter and Pfohl, 2016; Stellamanns et al., 2014; Tung et al., 2015; Uppaluri et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A major approach to simulating natural environments is seen in research on artificial microswimmers, where both the motile components and the confinement conditions can be controlled.
source: A major approach to simulating natural environments is seen in research on artificial microswimmers, where both the motile components and the confinement conditions can be controlled (Katuri et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The tsetse system can efficiently bridge in vivo analyses and artificial in vitro systems.
source: The tsetse system can efficiently bridge in vivo analyses and artificial in vitro systems.
evidence: This is a claim about the utility of the system.

claim: Many aspects of the natural environment can be described with sufficient precision to be mimicked by microfluidic structures.
source: We have shown that many aspects of the natural environment can be described with sufficient precision to be mimicked by microfluidic structures.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Any natural developmental stage can be isolated directly from the tsetse fly and studied in vitro, directly following in vivo analysis.
source: Furthermore, we can isolate any natural developmental stage directly from the tsetse fly and study it in vitro, directly following in vivo analysis.
evidence: This is a methodological advantage of the system.

claim: The data on three-dimensional morphologies and dynamic cellular waveforms gives a realistic assessment of the cellular preconditions for distinctive motile behaviour.
source: We have detailed on the three-dimensional morphologies of all microswimmer types and their dynamic cellular waveforms, which gives us a realistic assessment of the cellular preconditions for distinctive motile behaviour.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the morphometric and waveform analyses.

claim: The morphometric and waveform data is invaluable for deducing the swimming mechanism of a cell in a certain hydrodynamic or confined environment, including interactions with neighbouring cells.
source: This data is not only invaluable for deducing the swimming mechanism of a cell in a certain hydrodynamic or confined environment, including interactions with neighbouring cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the data.

claim: The data allows the development of quantitative mathematic models, as shown in advanced numerical simulations of bloodstream form trypanosomes.
source: It also allows the development of quantitative mathematic models, as we have previously shown in advanced numerical simulations of BSF trypanosomes (Alizadehrad et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The experimentally measured morphology of the mesocyclic stage agrees with the earlier in silico model.
source: The predictive power, especially of multi-particle collision dynamics simulations, is underlined by the fact that the experimentally measured morphology of the mesocyclic stage agrees with the earlier in silico model (Alizadehrad et al., 2015): the angle of the helical flagellar course around the mesocyclic cell body was predicted to be shallower than that of the BSF (or the procyclic form, compare Figure 5C with Figure 5A or I).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and demonstrated by the morphometric data.

claim: The overall aim of this work was to introduce a tractable in vivo microswimmer system and demonstrate the resolution and the precision of the methods available for studies therein.
source: The overall aim of this work was to introduce a tractable in vivo microswimmer system and demonstrate the resolution and the precision of the methods available for studies therein.
evidence: This is stated as the aim of the work.

claim: The interplay between cell body and flagellum generally needs to be taken into account for morphometry.
source: The interplay between cell body and flagellum generally needs to be taken into account for morphometry, for example in the search of an elusive resting state.
evidence: This is a methodological consideration.

claim: The maximum speed of a given morphotype is the most valuable parameter for assessing swimming capabilities.
source: Therefore, a straightforward parameter like median swimming speed turned out to be not instructive, instead we regard the maximum speed of a given morphotype as the most valuable parameter for assessing swimming capabilities (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on the data analysis.

claim: The flagellar beat frequencies were relatively constant in most cells of one type, suggesting that the specific morphology of the cell plays a role in defining basic parameters of flagellar beating.
source: Surprisingly, the flagellar beat frequencies were relatively constant in most cells of one type, suggesting that the specific morphology of the cell plays a role in defining basic parameters of flagellar beating.
evidence: This is an inference based on the waveform analysis.

claim: The physical factors of the surrounding environment impact on the beating pattern and determine absolute speed and direction of movement.
source: The physical factors of the surrounding environment then impact on this beating pattern and determine absolute speed and direction of movement.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observations.

claim: The results are in agreement with those obtained in the analysis of different trypanosome species, underlining the general relevance of the observations.
source: These results are in agreement with those obtained in the analysis of different trypanosome species (Bargul et al., 2016; Krüger and Engstler, 2016), underlining the general relevance of our observations.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The suggested impact of the cell body's properties on flagellar beating is consistent with a model of axonemal wave propagation control by mechanical bending forces, that is the geometric clutch hypothesis.
source: The suggested impact of the cell body´s properties on flagellar beating is consistent with a model of axonemal wave propagation control by mechanical bending forces, that is the geometric clutch hypothesis (Lindemann and Lesich, 2015; Lindemann, 1994a, 1994b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In the geometric clutch hypothesis model, dynein activity, causative of the curvature of flagella and cilia, is primarily controlled by mechanical forces acting transverse to the longitudinal arrangement of microtubules.
source: In this model, dynein activity, causative of the curvature of flagella and cilia, is primarily controlled by mechanical forces acting transverse to the longitudinal arrangement of microtubules.
evidence: This is a description of the geometric clutch hypothesis.

claim: In the case of the trypanosome flagellum, the attachment to the cell body would provide a permanent mechanical resistant force controlling the basic flagellar waveform.
source: In the case of the trypanosome flagellum, the attachment to the cell body would provide a permanent mechanical resistant force controlling the basic flagellar waveform.
evidence: This is an inference based on the geometric clutch hypothesis and the trypanosome morphology.

claim: The mechanical forces exerted by the environment should also have a direct impact on beat regulation.
source: On the other hand, the mechanical forces exerted by the environment should also have a direct impact on beat regulation, which we are primed to quantitatively analyse in microfluidic systems.
evidence: This is an inference and a statement about future research directions.

claim: Micropillar arrays were designed to mimic the microenvironment of the bloodstream and high-speed, single cell analysis allowed the direct observation of the trypanosomes behaviour upon mechanical resistance.
source: Here, micropillar arrays were designed to mimic the microenvironment of the bloodstream and high-speed, single cell analysis allowed the direct observation of the trypanosomes behaviour upon mechanical resistance.
evidence: This is a description of previous experimental setups.

claim: The design of microfluidic devices is readily adapted, in order to create topologies mimicking the microenvironments described in this work.
source: The design of such microfluidic devices is readily adapted, in order to create topologies mimicking the microenvironments described in this work.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Hypotheses on hydrodynamically controlled behaviour in certain compartments in the fly can be directly tested in the corresponding nature-inspired microflow chamber.
source: Thus, hypotheses on hydrodynamically controlled behaviour in certain compartments in the fly, for example, can be directly tested in the corresponding nature-inspired microflow chamber.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Microfluidic devices could be produced with elastic materials, which would allow the controlled application of forces on a confined population of parasites.
source: We envisage producing such structures with elastic materials, which would allow the controlled application of forces on a confined population of parasites.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The observed switching into synchronised flocks could be analysed using elastic microfluidic devices.
source: In this way, interesting collective behaviour like the observed switching into synchronised flocks could be analysed.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Controlled flow regimes in microfluidic devices would be compared with in vivo measurements, using fluorescent beads together with fluorescent cell lines in tracking experiments.
source: In the next step, the microfluidic devices would be connected to pump systems, in order to evaluate the behaviour of the parasites to hydrodynamic flow. Controlled flow regimes would be compared with in vivo measurements, using fluorescent beads together with fluorescent cell lines in tracking experiments (Figure 9, Video 9).
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Using the combination of flexible microfluidic devices and reversible microfluidic pump systems, even the analysis of peristaltic effects seems in reach.
source: Using the combination of flexible microfluidic devices and reversible microfluidic pump systems, even the analysis of peristaltic effects seems in reach.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The analysis of microswimmers in a biological system should be conducive to the elucidation of the patho-functional relevance of motile behaviour of specific parasite types.
source: Finally, the analysis of microswimmers in a biological system should be conducive to the elucidation of the patho-functional relevance of motile behaviour of specific parasite types.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential implications of the research.

claim: Motility data will help explain unresolved development processes, for example the journey of epimastigotes to the salivary glands or the crossing of the peritrophic matrix.
source: Motility data will help explain unresolved development processes, for example the journey of epimastigotes to the salivary glands or the crossing of the PM.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential implications of the research.

claim: The collective microswimmers produce significant forces, capable of moving tissues, raising questions about the influence of the large numbers of parasites accumulating in the fly on the surrounding microenvironment and on the trapped cells themselves.
source: The collective microswimmers produce significant forces, capable of moving tissues, thus raising the questions of what influence the amazing numbers of parasites accumulating in the fly have on the surrounding microenvironment and on the trapped cells themselves.
evidence: This is an observation and a statement about future research questions.

claim: The pleomorphic trypanosome strain EATRO 1125 (serodeme AnTat1.1) was used for this study.
source: For this study the pleomorphic trypanosome strain EATRO 1125 (serodeme AnTat1.1) (Le Ray et al., 1977) was used.
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: Procyclic cells were cultured at 27°C in SDM79 medium supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum and 20 mM glycerol.
source: Procyclic cells were cultured at 27°C in SDM79 medium (Brun and Schönenberger, 1979) supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (Hirumi and Hirumi, 1989) and 20 mM glycerol (Vassella et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: Male and female flies of Glossina morsitans morsitans were used in this study.
source: Male and female flies of Glossina morsitans morsitans were used in this study.
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: Flies were maintained in Roubaud cages at 27°C and 70% air humidity and fed with preheated defibrinated sheep blood through a silicon membrane three times a week.
source: Flies were maintained in Roubaud cages at 27°C and 70% air humidity and fed with preheated defibrinated sheep blood through a silicon membrane three times a week.
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.
